scenes.tts: The first film showed birds and bark sorting inherited moth colours. Can people shift a trait by choosing who reproduces? Keep the parent row, offspring row and changing trait frequency. The population picture still works.
scenes.caption: The first film showed birds and bark sorting inherited moth colours. Can people shift a trait by choosing who reproduces? Keep the parent row, offspring row and changing trait frequency. The population picture still works.
scenes.visual: Open on the first film's carried population strip: CREAM pale moths, BLUE-BLACK dark moths, RED predation paths and GREEN survivors on schematic bark. The bird-and-bark filter slides left. An empty TEAL-outlined filter appears beside it with a question mark. Reuse the first film's full COLOUR MAP without changes.
scenes.narration: The first film showed birds and bark sorting inherited moth colours. Can people shift a trait by choosing who reproduces? Keep the parent row, offspring row and changing trait frequency. The population picture still works.

scenes.visual: The two filters remain visible behind a brief title, 'Who Selects the Breeders?' The title folds into the TEAL filter, returning to the carried layout.

scenes.tts: Replace the moths with a row of plants that vary in an inherited trait. Some show the wanted form strongly. Others show it less. Their colours match the first film's map. Each plant keeps its inherited version of the trait.
scenes.caption: Replace the moths with a row of plants that vary in an inherited trait. Some show the wanted form strongly. Others show it less. Their colours match the first film's map. Each plant keeps its inherited version of the trait.
scenes.visual: The moth icons transform into simple plant cartoons in the same positions. BLUE-BLACK plants show the wanted form strongly; CREAM plants show it less. A label reads 'inherited variation'. Do not use measured heights, yields or counts. Each plant keeps its inherited colour as it grows; selection never recolours a parent. Keep the parent and offspring rows fixed in place and mark the scene 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Replace the moths with a row of plants that vary in an inherited trait. Some show the wanted form strongly. Others show it less. Their colours match the first film's map. Each plant keeps its inherited version of the trait.

scenes.tts: A farmer marks the plants with the wanted trait and saves seeds from those plants. The choice is deliberate. The choice changes who contributes offspring. Plants without the mark may grow, but their seeds are not used here.
scenes.caption: A farmer marks the plants with the wanted trait and saves seeds from those plants. The choice is deliberate. The choice changes who contributes offspring. Plants without the mark may grow, but their seeds are not used here.
scenes.visual: A farmer's hand places TEAL rings around BLUE-BLACK plants. Seed icons flow only from the ringed plants toward an empty offspring row. CREAM plants remain visible and healthy, but their seed paths stop at the TEAL choice gate.
scenes.narration: A farmer marks the plants with the wanted trait and saves seeds from those plants. The choice is deliberate. The choice changes who contributes offspring. Plants without the mark may grow, but their seeds are not used here.

scenes.tts: If the farmer repeats that choice, what should happen to the wanted inherited trait over generations? Watch the empty offspring rows before they fill.
scenes.caption: If the farmer repeats that choice, what should happen to the wanted inherited trait over generations? Watch the empty offspring rows before they fill.
scenes.visual: Hold the TEAL-ringed parent plants above several empty offspring rows. A question card asks, 'What becomes more common?' The BLUE-BLACK and CREAM legend pulses once; no offspring appear yet.
scenes.narration: If the farmer repeats that choice, what should happen to the wanted inherited trait over generations? Watch the empty offspring rows before they fill.

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Keep the question and empty rows visible. A thin ring timer advances while leaves on the parent plants move gently.

scenes.tts: The next row has a larger share of the wanted form. The selected form came from the starting variation. No plant changed its own inherited trait. The population changed because selected plants contributed more offspring to the next generation.
scenes.caption: The next row has a larger share of the wanted form. The selected form came from the starting variation. No plant changed its own inherited trait. The population changed because selected plants contributed more offspring to the next generation.
scenes.visual: Seeds pass through the TEAL gate and transform into an offspring row with a wider BLUE-BLACK section. Keep every parent icon unchanged. A bracket labelled 'trait frequency' expands over the BLUE-BLACK share, echoing the first film.
scenes.narration: The next row has a larger share of the wanted form. The selected form came from the starting variation. No plant changed its own inherited trait. The population changed because selected plants contributed more offspring to the next generation.

scenes.tts: Repeat the cycle: inherited variation, chosen breeders, then offspring. Across generations, the wanted trait becomes more common. The trait shifts without any organism choosing to change. This is artificial selection, when people choose which plants or animals breed.
scenes.caption: Repeat the cycle: inherited variation, chosen breeders, then offspring. Across generations, the wanted trait becomes more common. The trait shifts without any organism choosing to change. This is artificial selection, when people choose which plants or animals breed.
scenes.visual: Animate several schematic rows upward through the same TEAL gate. The BLUE-BLACK share grows without showing a measured rate. The cycle curls into a loop labelled 'artificial selection'; a small plant icon and animal icon sit beside 'plants or animals'.
scenes.narration: Repeat the cycle: inherited variation, chosen breeders, then offspring. Across generations, the wanted trait becomes more common. The trait shifts without any organism choosing to change. This is artificial selection, when people choose which plants or animals breed.

scenes.tts: Bring back the moth filter. In natural selection, conditions such as predators affect which inherited traits help organisms reproduce. In artificial selection, people choose the breeders. Both can shift inherited traits across generations. Neither process changes an organism during life.
scenes.caption: Bring back the moth filter. In natural selection, conditions such as predators affect which inherited traits help organisms reproduce. In artificial selection, people choose the breeders. Both can shift inherited traits across generations. Neither process changes an organism during life.
scenes.visual: Place the two carried filters side by side. Left: bark and bird with RED removal paths, label 'natural selection: conditions affect success'. Right: TEAL human-choice gate, label 'artificial selection: people choose breeders'. Identical arrows enter as 'inherited variation' and leave as 'shifted population'.
scenes.narration: Bring back the moth filter. In natural selection, conditions such as predators affect which inherited traits help organisms reproduce. In artificial selection, people choose the breeders. Both can shift inherited traits across generations. Neither process changes an organism during life.

scenes.tts: Both processes can shift a population in a few generations, while big changes usually take many. Inherited variation must be present, or first appear by chance, before selection can sort it.
scenes.caption: Both processes can shift a population in a few generations, while big changes usually take many. Inherited variation must be present, or first appear by chance, before selection can sort it.
scenes.visual: The two filters feed parallel schematic population strips. Each advances through several unlabeled generations, with every individual icon keeping its form. A small neutral sparkle adds a new variant before either filter. The labels 'variation first' and 'selection sorts it' move together beneath both strips.
scenes.narration: Both processes can shift a population in a few generations, while big changes usually take many. Inherited variation must be present, or first appear by chance, before selection can sort it.

scenes.tts: Natural selection also produces adaptations. An adaptation is a structure, function or behaviour shaped by natural selection that helps survival and reproduction. Its value depends on the environment around the organism.
scenes.caption: Natural selection also produces adaptations. An adaptation is a structure, function or behaviour shaped by natural selection that helps survival and reproduction. Its value depends on the environment around the organism.
scenes.visual: Return to the BLUE-BLACK moth carried from the first film. It receives a GREEN outline on sooty bark, then loses that outline when the bark turns pale. Three labels orbit it briefly: 'structure', 'function', 'behaviour'. Join them under 'adaptation shaped by natural selection'.
scenes.narration: Natural selection also produces adaptations. An adaptation is a structure, function or behaviour shaped by natural selection that helps survival and reproduction. Its value depends on the environment around the organism.

scenes.tts: Evolution is change in a population's inherited traits from one generation to the next. Natural selection is one cause of evolution. It is the cause that produces adaptations. Big changes usually build across many generations.
scenes.caption: Evolution is change in a population's inherited traits from one generation to the next. Natural selection is one cause of evolution. It is the cause that produces adaptations. Big changes usually build across many generations.
scenes.visual: Both population strips extend into a long horizontal sequence labelled 'generations'. A brace over any inherited shift reads 'evolution'. Highlight the natural-selection strip and connect it to 'adaptations'. Let the sequence continue beyond the frame to suggest many generations without showing a numeric scale.
scenes.narration: Evolution is change in a population's inherited traits from one generation to the next. Natural selection is one cause of evolution. It is the cause that produces adaptations. Big changes usually build across many generations.

scenes.tts: The shared pattern is unequal reproduction followed by inherited change. The important difference is what causes that unequal reproduction. In artificial selection, the cause is a person's choice. People shift inherited traits by choosing which organisms reproduce.
scenes.caption: The shared pattern is unequal reproduction followed by inherited change. The important difference is what causes that unequal reproduction. In artificial selection, the cause is a person's choice. People shift inherited traits by choosing which organisms reproduce.
scenes.visual: Merge the two filters into a comparison frame. The shared lower path reads 'unequal reproduction → inherited population change'. Above it, separate cause labels remain: 'environmental conditions' on the left and 'people's choices' in TEAL on the right. End with the TEAL path moving selected parents into the offspring row.
scenes.narration: The shared pattern is unequal reproduction followed by inherited change. The important difference is what causes that unequal reproduction. In artificial selection, the cause is a person's choice. People shift inherited traits by choosing which organisms reproduce.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex and one line only: 'People shift inherited traits by choosing which organisms reproduce.'
